text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Parliament approves reform of inheritance tax; asset tax to be scrapped next year
- Czech and German presidents call for European unity to be completed by admitting east European countries to EU
- Unemployment rises in October
- Government and opposition at odds over reduction in job promotion measures
- Small engineering firms fear industry association will fail to negotiate flexible sector pay deal
HANDELSBLATT
- Federal Labour Office wants 9.5 billion marks from Bonn in 1997 because of higher unemployment
- East German building sector goes into decline
- Lufthansa pilots threaten to strike
- Upper house may meet in special session to deal with 1997 tax bill
- President-designate of European Monetary Institute, Wim Duisenberg, says Maastricht must not be relaxed
- Daimler-Benz nine-month turnover rises
- Insurer Colonia discusses insurance cooperation with Postbank
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Volkswagen manager Lopez to be charged with industrial espionage
- Government to scrap subsidised state sector rents by 2005
- Defence ministry says it is having trouble maintaining equipment because of budget cuts
- One billion marks to be saved from social welfare budget in 1997
- Labour Office sees unemployment staying high
- Redundancies feared in health sector as controversy continues over health sector reform
- Bundesbank leaves rates unchanged
- Deutsche Telekom shares oversubscribed four or five times over
DIE WELT
- Parliament approves annual tax bill
- Czech and German presidents call for European unity to be completed by admitting east European countries to EU
- Coalition said to agree in principle to cut solidarity tax by two percentage points from 1998
- Airbus beats Boeing to USAir contract
- Unemployment rises despite improvement in economy
- IG Metall union and engineering employers overcome some differences in pay talks
- Employment promotion measures passed in parliament
- European Commission wants cut in west German shipbuilding capacity in order to help subsidised east German shipyards
